characterList.description: A middle-aged man with a mustache, wearing a light blue shirt and glasses. He is the VP of Research and Development at ExxonMobil.
characterList.name: Vijay Swarup

characterList.description: A young man wearing a white sweater and glasses. He is the Director of Quantum Hardware System Development at IBM.
characterList.name: Dr. Jerry Chow

content_metadata.description: A comprehensive exploration of the challenges in global energy supply, specifically the complexity of transporting liquefied natural gas (LNG), and how quantum computing can offer transformative solutions. The video features insights from Vijay Swarup of ExxonMobil and Dr. Jerry Chow of IBM, highlighting the need for innovation in computing to tackle these issues.

qAndA.answer: Efficient and reliable transportation, specifically shipping liquefied natural gas (LNG).
qAndA.question: What is the main challenge highlighted in relation to natural gas?
How many quantum computers does IBM currently have available through the cloud?

qAndA.answer: Classical bits represent either a 0 or a 1, while qubits can exist in a superposition of both states simultaneously, allowing for a much larger computational space.
qAndA.question: What is the key difference between classical and quantum bits?

qAndA.answer: The video starts with a neutral, curious mood, transitions to a somewhat anxious mood when describing the complexity of the problem, and then ends with a positive, hopeful tone as it introduces quantum computing as a potential solution.
qAndA.question: What is the overall mood of the video?

scenes.contextualRelevance: The use of diverse imagery highlights the interconnectedness of the challenges and the need for a global solution.

narrativeProgression.description: Establishes the global scale of the challenges being addressed.
Introduces Vijay Swarup and the dual challenge of energy supply and climate change.

props.name: Images of various landscapes and human activities (mountains, forests, oceans, cities, a solar farm, a gas burner, an incandescent light bulb, an industrial plant)

scenes.thematicElements: Global challenges, Energy supply, Climate change
scenes.title: Introduction to Global Energy Challenges

videoEditingDetails.description: Fast cuts between various images, creating a sense of dynamism and urgency.
Vijay Swarup appears on screen, speaking in a calm and measured tone.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The analogy of shipping LNG versus sneakers highlights energy transportation challenges and the comparison of decision numbers to atoms underscores problem scale.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Transition from visual - industrial structures to Milky Way, symbolizes problem size.
Transition from calm speech to thunder, emphasizes nature's unpredictability.

narrativeProgression.description: Discusses natural gas as an energy source and its environmental benefits compared to coal.
Highlights the challenges of shipping LNG and the complexity of the global supply chain.
Emphasizes the complexity due to larger fleets, weather disruptions, and demand fluctuations.

scenes.thematicElements: The need for efficient LNG shipping, The complexity of global supply chains, The limitations of traditional computing
scenes.title: The Complexity of LNG Transportation

videoEditingDetails.description: Close-up of a blue gas burner transitioning to a power button turning on, then to an incandescent light bulb lighting up.
Industrial structures and machinery are shown.
Animated graphic of planet Earth with shipping routes.
Transition to an image of the Milky Way galaxy.
Aerial shot of a large fleet of cargo ships.
Time-lapse of a thunderstorm over a city.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The phrase 'fresh set of eyes' emphasizes quantum computing's unique perspective and abstract animations illustrate classical vs quantum information processing.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Transition from modern hallway to quantum computer, shift from description to demonstration.
Visual shift from abstract computations to IBM processor emphasizes tangible quantum progress.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduces Dr. Jerry Chow and the concept of quantum computers.
Explains how quantum computers differ from classical computers.
Highlights IBM's advancements in quantum technology with a close-up of their processor chip.

scenes.thematicElements: The potential of quantum computing, The difference between classical and quantum bits, IBM's role in advancing quantum technology
scenes.title: The Advent of Quantum Computing

videoEditingDetails.description: Transition from space imagery to a bright, modern hallway.
Cut to a dark room with a quantum computer illuminated by blue lights.
Transition to abstract digital animations representing qubits and quantum computations.
Close-up of an IBM Quantum processor chip.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The mention of IBM's 300,000 users emphasizes the growing engagement and Swarup's final words about 'thinking differently' underscore quantum's transformative power.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Visualisation of quantum computing applications beyond an industry reinforces universality.

narrativeProgression.description: Swarup explains collaboration with IBM to solve LNG shipping using quantum computing.
Chow highlights IBM's quantum cloud accessibility and large user base.
Swarup concludes with optimism about quantum computing's future.

scenes.thematicElements: The collaboration between ExxonMobil and IBM, The democratization of quantum computing, The potential for quantum computing to transform various industries
scenes.title: Quantum Solutions for Global Challenges

videoEditingDetails.description: Cut back to footage of cargo ships.
Fast cuts between images of trucks, rideshare apps, and garbage trucks.
Cut back to the quantum computer, emphasizing its role.
Swarup reappears, concluding the video with a hopeful message.

climax.description: The video contains two climaxes within its structural narrative: The first climax is articulated by Vijay Swarup as he elucidates the futility of current computing systems to navigate the intricacies of the global LNG supply chain. The second is by Dr. Jerry Chow, who inspires hope with IBM's progress in quantum cloud computing and its vast user engagement.

storylines.description: The video navigates through two main storylines. It begins by introducing the global energy challenges, transitions into the detailed intricacies of LNG shipping, and culminates in the promise of quantum computing to provide solutions, emphasizing collaboration between ExxonMobil and IBM.

content_metadata.title: Unleashing Quantum Potential in Energy Solutions

trimmingSuggestions.description: The fast cuts between images could be shortened slightly without losing impact.
The visuals of industrial structures could be reduced, as they are less visually engaging than the animated Earth graphic.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: The challenges we face as a planet can be summed up simply. We need to provide a reliable
and affordable energy to our growing population while also addressing the risk of climate change.
Natural gas provides energy to the world. When compared to coal, it admits up to 60% fewer
greenhouse gases and produces fewer air pollutants for power generation. The issue isn't just one
of production, but also one of transportation. Shipping liquefied natural gas or LNG isn't like
shipping sneakers. Efficient shipping is absolutely critical. LNG needs to arrive on time
where people could run out of power. The global LNG industry today involves thousands of
voyages a year across the globe. To handle the scheduling in a global supply chain over a year,
you must account for the positions of each ship on each day of the year while satisfying
requirements for hundreds of deliveries across the world. This problem can involve millions of
discrete decisions, which means the number of routing combinations we would need to consider
could be larger than the number of atoms that exist in the universe. The problem becomes even
more challenging if you go to a much larger fleet or introduce uncertainty like disruptions
due to weather or fluctuations in the event. Then you're talking about billions or even trillions
of discrete decisions. There currently isn't a computer on the planet, powerful enough to do this
without greatly simplifying the problem. At least not yet.
Quantum computers allow us to view incredibly difficult problems with a fresh set of ice.
We've in condition in many cases, the simply not consider problems within an incredibly large
number of variables or potential solutions. Quantum computers completely change the model by which we
can perform information processing. Instead of with classical bits with zeros and ones,
we have quantum bits or qubits that follow the natural laws of quantum mechanics. The point is we're
not dealing with just flipping zeros and ones anymore and instead we have a rich set of rules that
governs our computations, allowing for the exploration of an exponentially larger computational space.
Working in partnership with IBM Quantum, Exxon Mobile Corporate Strategic Research has been
exploring how to model maritime inventory routing on quantum devices. We've looked at the
strengths of different mathematical approaches in quantum solvers, including how well they account for
complex real-world constraints, like limits on ship sizes and timing of when ships need to arrive
into part. These mathematical models could also be relevant to other vehicle routing problems,
including goods delivery, ride sharing services, and urban waste management.
Today, IBM already has over 20 quantum computers across the world running over 1 billion executions
a day on the IBM Cloud. We've opened up this technology so that everyone can sign up and experiment
with it. And so far, that means 300,000 users. By partnering with IBM Quantum,
our aim is to ultimately level up our ability to tackle more complex optimizations and make bigger
differences. We believe these will provide different ways of thinking about the dual challenge we
face now and the ones we will tackle in the foreseeable future.

youtube_description: ExxonMobil in partnership with IBM Quantum is researching how to use quantum algorithms to tackle the complexities of shipping. To watch Exxon's story and learn why other companies are partnering with IBM for quantum computing innovation, visit https://www.ibm.com/quantum-computing/case-studies/
youtube_title: ExxonMobil is exploring quantum computing to tackle complex energy challenges
